input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: a Content-Type parameter without an equals sign is stored with the value True instead of being skipped
- failure path: the header `text/html; charset` yields params['charset'] == True; get_encoding_from_headers (shown below the change) returns params['charset'].strip(...) which raises AttributeError on a bool, so reading response.text for such a response fails instead of falling back to ISO-8859-1

Reviewer finding
- description: A bare parameter with no '=' (e.g. Content-Type: text/html; charset) is now stored with the boolean value True, so get_encoding_from_headers calls .strip() on a bool and raises AttributeError.
- rationale: Trigger: a response whose Content-Type contains a bare 'charset' token without '='. The new code at line 520 sets params['charset']=True, and line 544 then calls True.strip(...), raising AttributeError. Previously such a token was skipped and the function fell back to ISO-8859-1 for text types. Impact: requests that read the encoding (e.g. response.text) crash on malformed but seen-in-the-wild headers instead of degrading gracefully.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label. A parameter with no '=' is stored as True, so get_encoding_from_headers calls .strip() on a bool and raises AttributeError. That makes response.text crash instead of falling back to ISO-8859-1.
